DATA_INGESTION.consequence: Without complete, timely cost data every other FinOps decision rests on partial numbers, and gaps surface only when the bill arrives.
DATA_INGESTION.evidence: Billing exports (for example FOCUS or the provider's detailed export) for every account and subscription for the last 3 months, with a completeness check.

ALLOCATION.consequence: Spend that is not allocated has no owner, so it cannot be charged back, costed per unit or reduced by the team that causes it.
ALLOCATION.evidence: Share of last month's cost allocated to an owner, measured by cost, with the allocation policy and the unallocated remainder.

REPORTING_ANALYTICS.consequence: Teams that cannot see their own cost cannot act on it, so decisions wait for central reports.
REPORTING_ANALYTICS.evidence: The cost views each group uses (engineering, product, finance) and the scheduled report list with its recipients.

ANOMALY_MANAGEMENT.consequence: Unexpected increases keep running until someone notices them, so the cost of a spike grows with the time it takes to detect and explain it.
ANOMALY_MANAGEMENT.evidence: The anomaly alert set-up and the last three alerts, with the time to triage and the cause found.

PLANNING_ESTIMATING.consequence: The running cost of new workloads is discovered after go-live, when changing the design is most expensive.
PLANNING_ESTIMATING.evidence: Cost estimates for two recent launches or changes, compared with their actual cost after launch.

FORECASTING.consequence: Forecast misses become budget surprises for finance and the board and weaken confidence in technology spend plans.
FORECASTING.evidence: Forecast against actual by quarter for the last 12 months, and the forecasting method.

BUDGETING.consequence: Without owner budgets and alerts, overspend is found at month end and nobody is accountable for the variance.
BUDGETING.evidence: Budgets by owner, the alert rules and the last variance review.

KPIS_BENCHMARKING.consequence: Without agreed measures, leaders cannot tell whether the practice is improving or compare progress with published data.
KPIS_BENCHMARKING.evidence: The KPI set with targets, and the last two leadership reviews of it.

UNIT_ECONOMICS.consequence: Without unit costs, spend growth cannot be separated from business growth, and pricing and product decisions ignore the cost to serve.
UNIT_ECONOMICS.evidence: Unit cost definitions and their trend for the main products or services.

ARCHITECTING_WORKLOAD_PLACEMENT.consequence: Design and placement choices fix most of the running cost before anyone reviews it.
ARCHITECTING_WORKLOAD_PLACEMENT.evidence: Architecture review records for recent designs showing the cost estimate and the comparison after go-live.

USAGE_OPTIMIZATION.consequence: Idle, oversized and always-on resources keep costing money every hour until someone acts on them.
USAGE_OPTIMIZATION.evidence: Provider-tool recommendation exports (rightsizing, idle) no older than 90 days, and the actions taken on them.

RATE_OPTIMIZATION.consequence: Steady usage paid at on-demand prices, or commitments that lapse or go unused, cost more per unit than necessary.
RATE_OPTIMIZATION.evidence: Commitment coverage and utilisation reports, the commitment register with expiry dates, and Spot usage.

LICENSING_SAAS.consequence: Unused licences and unmanaged renewals keep charging until the next renewal date has passed.
LICENSING_SAAS.evidence: The SaaS and licence inventory with owners, usage and renewal dates.

SUSTAINABILITY.consequence: Carbon and energy goals cannot be weighed against cost when the data is not used in decisions.
SUSTAINABILITY.evidence: Carbon or energy reports used in recent optimisation or placement decisions.

EXECUTIVE_STRATEGY_ALIGNMENT.consequence: Leadership cannot show the board that technology spend delivers its business case, so funding decisions rest on cost alone.
EXECUTIVE_STRATEGY_ALIGNMENT.evidence: Board or executive material linking cloud spend to business outcomes, and recorded trade-off decisions.

FINOPS_PRACTICE_OPERATIONS.consequence: Without an accountable owner and a regular review, cost actions depend on individual effort and stall when priorities change.
FINOPS_PRACTICE_OPERATIONS.evidence: The FinOps mandate, the named owner and sponsor, and the minutes of the last cost reviews.

GOVERNANCE_POLICY_RISK.consequence: Without enforced guardrails, the same cost problems recur in every new account and team.
GOVERNANCE_POLICY_RISK.evidence: Policy definitions (tags, regions, sizes, budgets) and their enforcement mode per account.

FINOPS_EDUCATION_ENABLEMENT.consequence: Engineers and product owners who are not trained in cost make decisions that undo the practice's gains.
FINOPS_EDUCATION_ENABLEMENT.evidence: Training records by role, and examples of recognised cost improvements.

INVOICING_CHARGEBACK.consequence: When cost is not reconciled and charged back, business units do not see what they spend and finance cannot rely on the numbers.
INVOICING_CHARGEBACK.evidence: Invoice reconciliation for the last month, and the chargeback or showback journal.

FINOPS_ASSESSMENT.consequence: Without periodic assessment, gaps in the practice are found by accident rather than by plan.
FINOPS_ASSESSMENT.evidence: The last practice assessment and its tracked improvement plan.

AUTOMATION_TOOLS_SERVICES.consequence: Manual tools and spreadsheets limit how much of the estate the practice can cover and how fast it can act.
AUTOMATION_TOOLS_SERVICES.evidence: The FinOps tool inventory with its integrations, and the routine actions that are automated.

INTERSECTING_DISCIPLINES.consequence: Procurement, asset management, security and architecture decide without cost data, and cost decisions are made without theirs.
INTERSECTING_DISCIPLINES.evidence: Shared processes or data feeds with ITAM, procurement, security, sustainability and architecture.

schedule.note: A finding starts at its wave's window (DESIGN.md 5.4: wave 1 from month 0, wave 2 from month 3, wave 3 from month 9) and never before every finding it depends on has reached its first milestone: 3 months after that finding starts, or its whole target duration if shorter (F3 re-review R1). A capability gap moves one level at a time: the first level at firstMilestoneMonths, each further level levelStepMonths later, so its duration grows with the gap and severity sets only the order (M4 CIO challenge D4; the FinOps Foundation describes maturity as iterative, Crawl to Walk to Run). durationMonths applies to the other findings. Spreading Critical work by delivery capacity is F7.

decisions.question: MP-01
decisions.title: Appoint an accountable FinOps owner with a mandate
decisions.consequence: Until someone is accountable for cloud and technology spend, no one is responsible for seeing this programme through.
decisions.action: Appoint an accountable FinOps owner with a written mandate and an executive sponsor
decisions.evidence: The appointment and the written mandate, with the executive sponsor named.
decisions.actionUnconfirmed: Confirm who is accountable for cloud and technology spend; if no one is, appoint an accountable FinOps owner with a written mandate and an executive sponsor
